import html # Pre‑defined HTML template with named placeholders. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title} – Invitation
{event_title}
Date: {event_date}
{event_description}
{notes_section} """ def create_event_invitation(e_title: str, e_description: str, e_date: str, e_notes: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized HTML representation of an event invitation. Parameters ---------- e_title : str The name or heading of the event. e_description : str A detailed description of the event. May contain newlines and formatting. e_date : str The date on which the event is scheduled. e_notes : str Any additional information or instructions provided by the user. Returns ------- str A fully escaped, well‑formed HTML string ready for safe rendering. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is empty or consists only of whitespace. """ # Basic validation: ensure mandatory fields are present for name, value in (("Title", e_title), ("Description", e_description), ("Date", e_date)): if not value or not value.strip(): raise ValueError(f"{name} cannot be empty.") # Escape all user‑supplied content to prevent XSS and other injection escaped_title = html.escape(e_title, quote=True) escaped_description = html.escape(e_description, quote=True) escaped_date = html.escape(e_date, quote=True) # Handle optional notes: only include the section if there is meaningful content if e_notes and e_notes.strip(): escaped_notes = html.escape(e_notes, quote=True) notes_section = f'
Notes: {escaped_notes}
' else: notes_section = '' # Safely format the template with the escaped values invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=escaped_title, event_date=escaped_date, event_description=escaped_description, notes_section=notes_section ) return invitation_html
